questions.question: What is the BEST approach to remediating the cloud workload runtime detection gap?
questions.scenario_context: A SaaS firm's IR-driven security review reveals: 23 of 47 microservices in the production Kubernetes cluster have no runtime detection (Falco) deployed. A recent breach (now contained) exploited one of these unprotected services — undetected for 6 days before customer reports surfaced. The CISO + CTO + AppSec + SRE + Platform Engineering coordinating remediation strategy. Cluster supports 2.4M end-users + handles payment processing (PCI scope).

options.A: Issue a formal PCI DSS exception for the 23 services without runtime detection; document the gap in the firm's exception registry for the next external audit.
options.B: Deploy Falco runtime detection only on the 23 services that are currently missing it; the existing 24 are already covered with the current Falco DaemonSet deployment.
options.C: Migrate the entire Kubernetes cluster to a managed service such as EKS-Anywhere or GKE Autopilot; these managed services include runtime detection capability by default at the platform layer.
options.D: Enable Falco across all 47 microservices + verify ATT&CK coverage + alert routing to SIEM + AppSec-SRE shared responsibility + detection-as-code Falco rules + post-incident review + customer impact + regulator notification + post-incident coverage policy.

questions.key_concept: Cloud workload runtime detection gap = enable Falco across all + verify ATT&CK coverage + alert routing to SIEM + AppSec-SRE shared responsibility + detection-as-code Falco rules + post-incident review + customer impact + regulator notification + post-incident coverage gap policy. Nine tracks.
questions.pre_read: For runtime detection gap questions, anchor on coverage-completion + verification + governance framework. Exception-for-gap, deploy-only-gap-without-verification, and migration-as-shortcut framings each fail.
questions.correct_explanation: NIST SP 800-190 (Application Container Security Guide), CIS Kubernetes Benchmark, CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance, Falco / Sysdig Secure / Aqua Cloud Workload Protection documentation, and PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 11 + 12.10 establish runtime detection gap remediation. Nine tracks: (1) ENABLE FALCO ACROSS ALL 47 MICROSERVICES — DaemonSet pattern; covers all nodes + their pods; (2) VERIFY RUNTIME DETECTION COVERAGE MAPS TO MITRE ATT&CK — gap analysis; especially T1611 (Escape to Host), T1486 (Data Encrypted for Impact), T1078 (Valid Accounts); (3) ALERT ROUTING TO SIEM — Falco alerts integrated with SIEM for correlation + analyst triage; (4) APPSEC-SRE SHARED RESPONSIBILITY MODEL — Falco is a workload-runtime control owned by AppSec + operated by SRE; cross-team responsibility; (5) DETECTION-AS-CODE FOR FALCO RULES — rules in Git; PR review; testing; (6) POST-INCIDENT REVIEW — why were 23 services missing Falco? deployment-process gap? team-ownership gap? policy enforcement gap?; (7) CUSTOMER IMPACT — 6-day detection delay; data exposure analysis; (8) REGULATOR NOTIFICATION — PCI DSS 12.10 incident reporting; state breach laws; SEC Reg S-K Item 1.05 if material; (9) POST-INCIDENT DETECTION-COVERAGE GAP POLICY — runtime detection mandatory for all production services; admission controller enforces; gap = block deployment.

wrong_explanations.A: Failure mode = EXCEPTION-FOR-PCI-GAP. PCI DSS 12.10 requires incident response capability including detection; an exception that documents 'we don't detect runtime threats on 23 services' fails 11.3 vulnerability management and 12.10. QSA will flag this as material finding; remediation, not exception, is required.
wrong_explanations.B: Failure mode = DEPLOY-ONLY-23-WITHOUT-VERIFICATION. The 24 already-covered services may have Falco rules outdated, not aligned to current ATT&CK techniques, or with deployment gaps. Re-verify coverage across ALL 47 + remediate gaps; not just close the obvious gap.
wrong_explanations.C: Failure mode = MIGRATION-AS-REMEDIATION-SHORTCUT. Migrating to managed Kubernetes is a multi-quarter project; doesn't address the immediate gap (23 unprotected services NOW). Migration may be appropriate long-term, but remediation comes first.

tips: Trap is A — 'issue formal PCI DSS exception' is candidate-seductive because exceptions are a real PCI DSS mechanism; but PCI DSS 11 + 12.10 require incident response capability including detection. Exception that documents 'we don't detect runtime threats' fails the requirement; QSA will flag as material finding. Remediation, not exception.

Cloud workload runtime detection gap = enable Falco all services + verify ATT&CK coverage + alert routing + AppSec-SRE shared model + detection-as-code + post-incident review + customer impact + regulator notification + post-incident coverage policy. Nine tracks.

Exam-day shortcut: when stem describes CLOUD WORKLOAD RUNTIME DETECTION GAP IN PCI SCOPE, look for coverage-completion + governance framework; exception-for-gap, deploy-only-gap, and migration-as-shortcut framings each fail.
